author: KA (Khurram)
headline: Google tests a cuffless smartwatch check for high blood pressure
text: A Google study suggests an ordinary smartwatch can flag likely high blood pressure without anyone strapping on a cuff first. The paper appeared in Nature, and in a trial with 196 adults the watch picked up more hypertension cases than a single reading at a doctor's office did. The numbers are modest, and Google says so. The watch caught 65.8% of the people who truly had hypertension, against 55.3% for the initial office screening, while specificity (correctly clearing healthy people) was 90%. When the watch said 'high', it was right 80.6% of the time, compared with 77.8% for office readings. The system uses two sensors nearly every smartwatch has: the optical pulse sensor and the accelerometer. Google Research says the accelerometer also picks up tiny vibrations of the wrist caused by each heartbeat. Google puts the number of hypertension sufferers worldwide above one billion and says most are unaware of it, especially people aged 18 to 44. The full results are in the Nature paper.
